dedupe_keys.name: fcc consumer complaints data consumer help center

description: This dataset gives the individual informal complaints that consumers file with the FCC Consumer Help Center, from 31 October 2014 onwards, with about 3.7 million rows by September 2026. Each complaint has a ticket number, the dates of the issue and of the ticket, the method of filing, the issue category (such as unwanted calls, billing, availability including rural call completion, equipment, privacy, robocalls and telemarketing), the type of service (phone, internet, TV, radio), the form used, and the location as city, state and ZIP code centre point. Coverage: the United States, daily updates. Format and access: a table through the Socrata API with CSV and JSON export and a map of complaints by state, free as US government data. Caveats: the FCC does not verify the facts consumers allege; the data reflect what consumers select; most complaints are about unwanted calls, not network failures. Simulation uses: crowdsourced reports of service availability problems, for example after storms, for service performance baselines and for checking how outages are experienced by users. Related records: FCC DIRS status reports give provider-side outage data, and Arcep's J'alerte l'Arcep gives a French counterpart.
